Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: 2027 NFL draft rankings: Jordan Reid's top 50 prospects, scouting reports
stories.summary: Jordan Reid unveils his debut rankings for the 2027 NFL draft class with 50 players -- including six quarterbacks and an elite wide receiver prospect.
stories.body:
With the 2026 college football season in full swing, it's time to start stacking the top prospects in the 2027 NFL draft class, which begins on April 29 in Washington, D.C. I've been watching and evaluating these players for a couple of years in some instances, and these rankings are a compilation of my scouting (both on film and in person) and conversations I've been having with scouts and evaluators around the NFL.

We're going to start these rankings with 50 players, with scouting reports on the top 25, but this list will expand as the draft gets closer and closer. And these rankings will evolve -- some players will shoot up boards, others will fall and still more will ultimately return to school for another year. But this is how I currently see things in the 2027 class.

Let's get to it, starting with arguably the best wide receiver prospect of the past 15-20 years. Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk, and the top names at every position are listed at the bottom.

Jump to:

Rankings by position

1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State*
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 222

Stats through Oct. 17: 52 receptions for 984 receiving yards (18.9 yards per catch) and 12 touchdowns

Smith could have All-Pro potential early in his NFL career as a true No. 1 receiver. He immediately changes the offensive outlook for the team that adds him. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And he's equally as capable of winning with strength at the catch point. Smith's change of direction in routes needs to become sharper, as he can take too many choppy steps when working back toward passers. But he is tough to stop when allowed to attack defenses vertically.

2. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame*
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 197

Stats through Oct. 17: 13 tackles, five passes defensed, 40% completion percentage allowed

With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect. His length and physicality allow him to excel when getting hands on receivers in press man coverage. He also has the awareness to identify and defend route concepts in zone coverage. Moore has the ball skills to match receivers, routinely tracking and attacking the ball out of the air. But he needs to improve his discipline and hand timing at the top of routes.

3. Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina*
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 250

Stats through Oct. 17: five tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, two forced fumbles

With a slender frame, Stewart has rare burst and closing speed as a pass rusher. That allows him to wreak havoc on twists and stunts, though the tools have yet to lead to high-end production at the college level. And he might not have many chances to add to his tape, as he's currently suspended from the team. Stewart must also become more consistent with using his length and shedding against the run.

4. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 246

Stats through Oct. 17: 25 tackles, 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery

Simmons is an energetic and high-effort pass rusher, with a quick first step to explode past blockers. He has a nifty combination of hesitation moves and shoulder fakes. But he still needs to develop consistent counter moves, as he can get stuck if his initial move isn't effective. Simmons is a powerful run defender, using a strong base and powerful hands to keep his frame clean when setting the edge. Simmons could miss time with a high-ankle sprain suffered Oct. 17 against Florida.

5. Chris Cole, LB, Georgia*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 235

Stats through Oct. 17: 40 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 8.5 tackles for loss, two fumble recoveries, three passes defensed

Cole is an easy moving, urgent defender from the second level. He has excellent lateral agility and pursuit speed to close on ball carriers in a hurry. But his ability to read and react to run concepts is still a work in progress, as his eyes can get fixated in the wrong spots. And he can be slow at recognizing concepts in zone coverage, leading to easy catches in his area. Cole is frequently used as a blitzer, which he does effectively.

6. Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana*
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 208

Stats through Oct. 17: 39 receptions for 684 receiving yards (17.8 yards per catch) and eight touchdowns

Becker is primarily used as a vertical threat, and there are few college players who can match his straight-ahead speed. But he is more than just a threat with his legs; he's similar to an NBA rebounder with the way he wins 50-50 passes. That ability comes from a combination of elite body control at the catch point and A-plus hand-eye coordination, which helps him see the ball in slow motion. Becker does need to round out his route tree, showing NFL teams that he has more branches on it than just vertical patterns.

7. Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson*
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 205

Stats through Oct. 17: 19 tackles, one interception for 2 yards, nine passes defensed, 24% completion percentage allowed

Hampton is a physically imposing cornerback who strives to humiliate receivers at the line of scrimmage by getting his hands on them. Since most receivers struggle to untangle from his coverage, he would be ideal for press man coverage schemes at the next level. Hampton is also a forceful tackler on the perimeter, with lots of knockback strength when coming into contact with ball carriers. But he does need to be more disciplined with his timing in coverage.

8. Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 215

Stats through Oct. 17: 136-of-203 passing (67.0% completion percentage) for 1,940 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions; 21 carries for 142 rushing yards (6.8 yards per carry) and two touchdowns

Mestemaker is my top quarterback prospect despite this being only his second season as a starter in high school and college. He has an unconventional style, holding the ball at his waistline before ripping a fiery, three-quarters release. Mestemaker has the confidence to test the tightest of windows from various platforms, but that can get the best of him and lead to turnovers. Plus, he can be oblivious to underneath defenders. Mestemaker is bit of a streaky passer, though his hot streaks feature plenty of "wow" moments. And he is capable of being a running threat.

9. Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 315

Stats through Oct. 17: 18 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four tackles for loss, three passes defensed,

An explosive 3-technique, Echoles is one of the most versatile and well-conditioned interior defenders in the country. He has energetic hands that help him accelerate past blockers, and reliable lower body strength helps him be a malleable run defender. Echoles still needs to make major improvements in his counter moves, as he can get stuck on blockers when his power and initial moves are matched. Plus, he can get caught not being firm on contact and get moved off his spot.

10. Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia*
Height: 6-0 | Weight: 180

Stats through Oct. 17: 13 tackles, one interception for 0 yards, five passes defensed, 45.8% completion percentage allowed

Robinson is an ultra-athletic cornerback whose quick feet and sudden change of direction helps him stay connected in man coverage. But there are times when Robinson gives up big gains because his technique tends to be abandoned. His best reps come in zone coverage, where he has a great feel for concepts unfolding. Robinson has excellent awareness with attacking the ball in flight, and he has a linebacker-like appetite for contact in run support.

11. Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee*
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 305

Stats through Oct. 17: 22 tackles, five sacks, 9.5 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, two passes defensed

Gilliam is an explosive, up-field interior defender who can penetrate the first level with ease. His game centers around quickness, as his first step is difficult for blockers to match. Gilliam's active hands help him win with multiple plans of attack in pass-rush situations. He is equally as strong as a run defender, anchoring his feet in the ground to withstand at the point of attack. He also can stack and dislodge blocking attempts to knock run concepts off-schedule.

12. Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU*
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 307

Stats through Oct. 17: 452 snaps, 1.3% pressure rate allowed, 1.0% blown run block rate

Seaton combines a good blend of awareness, quick hands and lower-body suddenness to be a high-level pass protector. He's also an easy mover in space, which allows him to excel as a puller or on screen plays. Seaton can be trusted on an island, but his biggest area of improvement must come as a run blocker. His hands and feet are inconsistent when driving on blocks to the second level.

13. Greg Johnson, OG, Minnesota
Height: 6-6 | Weight: 325

Stats through Oct. 17: 343 snaps, 0.5% pressure rate allowed, 0% blown run block rate

Johnson is a hulking interior blocker whose strength helps him latch and sustain at the point of attack. He has a reliable anchor that helps him tether his feet and quickly stall pass-rush moves. In gap run schemes, Johnson has shown quickness when pulling. In zone run schemes, Johnson can be fluid enough to climb and cover up linebackers on the second level. A lot of Johnson's losses are a result of him relying solely on his upper body to generate torque and movement. His recovery athleticism is average, and he can face challenges when forced to readjust after being beaten quickly around either shoulder.

14. Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah
Height: 6-8 | Weight: 305

Stats through Oct. 17: 381 snaps, 0% pressure rate allowed, 0.5% blown run block rate

Williams' playing style is a bit unconventional and his lack of experience shows throughout games. However, he has plenty of skills that NFL teams covet. Williams' towering frame helps him shadow and shut down pass rushers around the arc of the pocket. His lower-body fluidity and drive strength at the point of attack allows him to gain momentum into blocks as a run blocker. His knee bend must become more consistent throughout reps, and he'll also have moments where he lacks depth in pass protection sets.

15. Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss
Height: 6-0 | Weight: 205

Stats through Oct. 17: 142-of-210 passing (67.6%) for 1,676 passing yards and 14 touchdowns to four interceptions; 36 carries for 127 rushing yards (3.5 yards per carry) and six touchdowns

A headache for the opposition in multiple ways, Chambliss can break down defenses with both his throwing ability and mobility. His excellent field vision complements a compact and fiery release, helping him anticipate and attack over the middle. Despite his lack of size, he can consistently reach all areas of the field. Chambliss also isn't afraid to welcome high-leverage moments, which he showed throughout last year's College Football Playoff and so far this season. His frame and age (he'll be 25 years old before next season) could inhibit his draft profile.

16. Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida*
Height: 6-1 | Weight: 225

Stats through Oct. 17: 135 carries for 763 rushing yards (5.7 yards per carry) and 13 touchdowns; nine receptions for 59 receiving yards (6.6 yards per catch)

Baugh is the top running back prospect in this class, a chiseled and powerful runner with timely short-area quickness. He activates his lower body to slither his way through creases, while also being able to simply plant his foot and accelerate through the line of scrimmage. Baugh doesn't have the home run speed to rattle off long touchdowns, but he has enough to generate explosive plays with the yardage that's available to him. He has a lot of work to do as a pass protector, showing inconsistency with his technique and in recognizing blitzing defenders.

17. Darian Mensah, QB, Miami*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 205

Stats through Oct. 17: 135-of-167 passing (80.8%) for 1,764 passing yards and 18 touchdowns to one interception; 15 carries for 85 rushing yards (5.7 yards per carry) and two touchdowns

Mensah is a locate-and-loft thrower who has a great sense of true progressions and can string together long stretches of accurate completions. He has great touch on passes, as he can drop throws right into the outstretched arms of targets. Mensah is also unafraid to throw into the teeth of blitzes and make defenses pay for trying to rush his throw plans. He is sufficient enough with his legs to buy time and make throws outside of structure. But Mensah has average velocity when forced to throw into tight windows. And he needs to improve his ball security, as rushers have had success jarring the ball loose from him in the pocket.

18. Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana*
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 210

Stats through Oct. 17: 32 receptions for 585 receiving yards (18.3 yards per catch) and seven touchdowns

Built like a running back, Marsh's separators are his frame, competitiveness and power at the catch point. His strong releases at the line help him work through and steer clear of press coverage prior to making catches. And he's excellent after the catch, turning underneath catches into big gains as defenders bounce off his frame. Marsh is also an outstanding run blocker who isn't afraid of doing the dirty work inside of the box. The one issue with Marsh is that he has yet to develop other tactics to establish and maintain true separation.

19. Yhonzae Pierre, Edge, Alabama
Height: 6-3 | Weight: 251

Stats through Oct. 17: 23 tackles, 3.5 sacks, 4.5 tackles for loss, one forced fumble, three passes defensed, one interception for 27 yards and a touchdown

Pierre is an aggressive defender whose pursuit energy has very little drop-off throughout games. He is equally as effective from a stand-up outside linebacker position or with his hand in the ground. Pierre is a true havoc creator on stunts and twists, using overwhelming strength to get blockers. As a run defender, he can stand his ground and be a consistent edge setter. But he is more of a build-up rusher than true bender, which limits his amounts of clean wins against offensive tackles.

20. Lance Heard, OT, Kentucky
Height: 6-6 | Weight: 325

Stats through Oct. 17: 436 snaps, 2.3% pressure rate allowed, 1.5% blown run block rate

Heard is a physical, wide-framed blocker who uses his natural tools effectively. His physicality is always turned up to the max, as he seeks to destroy anything in his path as a true road grader. He has excellent knockback strength, and defenders jolt back when he's able to get proper hand placement. Heard has average range as a pass protector and quick up-field rushers have had success clearing his near hip to create pathways to pressure passers. He also could be a converted to guard to maximize his strength levels in confined areas.

21. CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame*
Height: 6-2 | Weight: 215

Stats through Oct. 17: 129-of-193 passing for 1,639 passing yards and 16 touchdowns to one interception; 23 carries for 82 rushing yards (3.6 yards per carry) and three touchdowns

Carr is a refined pocket passer whose eyes, feet and throwing motion are always in cohesion. With an easy throwing motion, he is a decisive passer who trusts his eyes to pick apart defenses. He has a great feel for the types of passes that are needed, putting enough touch or velocity on them. And he is routinely in control at the line of scrimmage with protections and when calling audibles. Carr's overall arm strength and velocity are average. And he sometimes creates chaotic negative losses trying to make a positive play instead of moving on to the next play.

22. Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 205

Stats through Oct. 17: 21 tackles, six passes defensed, 29.4% completion percentage allowed

Jones is a slender corner who has shielding length on the perimeter. His angular build helps him excel in coverage, where he can utilize his frame on a vertical plane. Jones has good hips and vertical speed to stay hip-to-hip with receivers. His wingspan makes it challenging for receivers to clear his coverage and access throwing windows. Jones can play man coverage in spurts, but his traits are glorified in zone coverage. He still needs to add strength and mass, and his consistency as a wrap-up-and-finish tackler also must improve.

23. Jamari Johnson, TE, Oregon
Height: 6-5 | Weight: 255

Stats through Oct. 17: 17 receptions for 224 receiving yards (13.2 yards per catch) and two touchdowns

Johnson is a big playmaker in the passing game, especially over the middle of the field. He has natural hands and the catch radius to pluck balls outside his frame. As a route runner, Johnson wins with controlled tempos, decisiveness and spatial awareness. He can compete through contact when challenged, but he won't surprise defenders with his top-end speed or suddenness. Johnson also isn't a dynamic threat who can stack up extra yards after the catch that aren't created for him schematically. He isn't overly reliable on single blocks as a run blocker.

24. Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri*
Height: 6-4 | Weight: 220

Stats through Oct. 17: 132-of-209 passing (63.2%) for 1,773 passing yards and 14 touchdowns to two interceptions; 20 carries for 18 yards (0.9 yards per carry)

Simmons has a slight build but is an extremely explosive thrower with A-level arm strength. His baseball pitching background shows, as he has a whippy and violent throwing motion that adds excellent velocity to his passes. There isn't a window on the field that isn't attainable thanks to his arm strength. Simmons is also an anticipatory thrower who is consistent in making "about to be open" throws to targets. He is also capable of executing touch throws and can layer the ball into receivers. Simmons can use his powerful arm as a crutch, as he can be late to some reads and with getting the ball out when pressured. Simmons' physical tools are tantalizing, but the sample size is still very small.

Bolden plays a variety of spots in Georgia's secondary but projects best as a center field free safety. He is a mistake eraser in the back end, showcasing range and instinctiveness to quickly bring a halt to plays. Bolden is an aggressive tackler who comes downhill with urgency. His lack of strength can hurt him in man coverage, as bigger receivers can outmuscle him and make catches through his frame.

stories.headline: Mbappé and Diomande delight, Vinícius Jr. whistled in Real Madrid win
stories.summary: José Mourinho said Real Madrid's fans "went home happy" thanks to stunning goals from Yan Diomande and Kylian Mbappé in the team's 4-1 win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- José Mourinho said Real Madrid's fans "went home happy" thanks to stunning goals from Yan Diomande and Kylian Mbappé in the team's 4-1 win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

A close-fought first half saw Madrid go in ahead at the break thanks to Bernardo Silva's goal, before the home side pulled away at the Bernabéu thanks to Arda Güler, Mbappé and Diomande.

- Source: Barça report PSG to UEFA for 'overly aggressive' tifo

- Carrick hits back at Fernandes criticism after Como rout Man United

Madrid's record signing Diomande replaced Vinícius Júnior -- who again drew some whistles from the crowd -- on 70 minutes and delivered the game's highlight, volleying Brahim Díaz's pass into the top corner.

It was Diomande's third goal in his last four games for Real Madrid, after failing to score in his first eight appearances since his transfer from Leipzig worth a potential €140 million ($189m) this summer. The Ivory Coast international also had an assist on Mbappé's goal.

"The fans went home happy, watching the duo of Mbappé and Diomande," Mourinho said after the match. "They bought their tickets, and they go home happy."

Mourinho denied that he'd introduced Diomande with Sunday's LaLiga Clasico in mind, with Vinícius suspended for the clash in Barcelona.

"The intention wasn't thinking about the Clasico, it was thinking about this game," the coach said. "I knew a fresh Diomande, coming on with half an hour left, is difficult [to handle]. His speed is important."

"For me, Vini had a good game," he added. "Tactically, for his coach, he had a good game ... He could have scored a great goal, and their keeper made a great save. I wouldn't say he's sad, that's a feeling only he can explain, but his coach is happy."

"If he [Vini] is sad, it's because he wants to give a lot to the team, and to the fans," Mbappé told Movistar. "He needs to be calm, and proud of who he is. A great player has to be proud of who he is. His confidence will come back, because he has the quality."

Speaking later in his post-match news conference, Mourinho said the fans' whistling of Vinícius was unhelpful in the player's quest to find his best form.

The winger has been frequently targeted by some fans at the Bernabéu over the last year, even after signing a new long-term deal in the summer.

"When you're whistled away from home, it's a source of motivation," Mourinho said. "When you're whistled at home, it hurts you."

stories.headline: 2026 MLB offseason manager changes: Tracking hirings, firings
stories.summary: The offseason carousel is in motion. Here's who is out -- and who could be in line to replace them.
stories.body:
The first 100-loss season in Los Angeles Angels franchise history meant the end of the line for skipper Kurt Suzuki.

The second managerial change since the end of the regular season came Monday when the Angels announced they would not pick up Suzuki's 2027 club option and will instead begin a search for a new manager.

Suzuki joins Dan Wilson, who told reporters last month he would not be returning as skipper of the Seattle Mariners.

Which major league teams will change managers next? And who could be next in line?

ESPN will track all of the managerial hirings and firings -- and provide potential top replacements for every opening as they happen.

Los Angeles Angels
2026 manager: Kurt Suzuki (Oct. 21)

Suzuki lasted just one year as Angels skipper.

A former catcher, Suzuki played the final two of his 16 big-league seasons (2021-22) with the Angels, then signed a one-year deal to manage the team last October.

Los Angeles' 62-100 mark in 2026 represented the first 100-loss season in franchise history, and a 10-game drop-off from the 2025 team, managed by Ron Washington and Ray Montgomery.

Longtime Angels owner Arte Moreno sold the club to Stan Kroenke in September. Kroenke won't officially take over until the first quarter of 2027.

Whether interim general manager John Mozeliak will continue with the team remains to be seen.

Seattle Mariners
2026 manager: Dan Wilson (Sept. 27)

Wilson is out in his second full season in Seattle after being hired in August 2024 to replace Scott Servais.

The Mariners entered the 2026 season as division favorites and a potential top American League contender coming off a 2025 playoff run that saw them eight outs away from the franchise's first World Series appearance before falling to the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the ALCS. Seattle got off to a slow start, with just four wins in its first 13 games. With season-long struggles from big stars like Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez, coupled with inconsistent pitching and an underperforming offense, the Mariners never got to more than four games over .500 on the season.

"This season has been very difficult, and of course the results have not been what any of us had expected," Wilson said after Sunday's 7-3 win over the Angels. "As a result, it was concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners."

Arsenal have joined the race to sign Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, while Crystal Palace duo Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are on the radar of Manchester United ahead of the January transfer window. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Arsenal have joined the race to sign Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, according to The Sun. The 22-year-old has caught the eye of Europe's top clubs following his UEFA Champions League hat trick against Internazionale, as Mikel Arteta looks to bolster his attacking options. The Gunners are also in the final stages of negotiations with midfielder Declan Rice over a new long-term contract, according to Fabrizio Romano.

- Manchester United are monitoring Crystal Palace duo Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ahead of the January transfer window, TEAMtalk reports. Both players face uncertain contract situations, with Mateta's deal expiring in 2027 and while Sarr has a deal until 2029, he is weighing up a new offer from Palace amid interest. United are also set to bring in a left back next summer, with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert being scouted, according to iNews.

- Barcelona have ruled out a January exit for versatile youngster Xavi Espart, per TEAMtalk. Despite heavy interest from Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, a fresh contract for the 19-year-old through 2030 has secured his long-term future at Camp Nou. Espart is a natural midfielder but has been deployed as a full back on either side this season as he made the breakthrough into the first XI.

- Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez is set to leave the club at the end of the season, according to The Daily Mail. Last week, Martinez, 28, criticized the United hierarchy over their recent record in the transfer market and later apologized, but the Argentina international's future has now been cast into serious doubt.

- Tottenham Hotspur right back Pedro Porro would "seriously consider" a move to Barcelona or Real Madrid, reports Football Insider. Despite signing a contract extension until 2031, the 27-year-old is enticed by the prospect of competing for trophies and playing in the Champions League in Spain.

Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.
